Q: Is there a quick change tabs function in Visual Studio Code? A:

2020: Another way to quickly change tabs would be in VSCode 1.45 (April 2020)

Switch tabs using mouse wheel

When you use the mouse wheel to scroll over editor tabs, you can currently not switch to the tab, only reveal tabs that are out of view.

Now with a new setting workbench.editor.scrollToSwitchTabs this behaviour can be changed if you change it to true.

Note: you can also press and hold the Shift key while scrolling to get the opposite behaviour (i.e. you can switch to tabs even with this setting being turned off).

Update 2026: scrolling the tab strip without switching tabs

Following yeliabsalohcin's comment, note that "workbench.editor.scrollToSwitchTabs": false is intended to let the mouse wheel scroll/reveal the tab strip without opening another tab. Holding Shift while scrolling temporarily switches tabs instead.

For "out of view" tabs, VSCode 1.104 (Aug. 2025) also added workbench.editor.titleScrollbarVisibility. For example:

{
    "workbench.editor.scrollToSwitchTabs": false,
    "workbench.editor.titleScrollbarVisibility": "visible",
    "workbench.editor.titleScrollbarSizing": "large"
}

That keeps a usable horizontal scrollbar available for browsing hidden tabs, but without selecting them.

Another option, available since VSCode 1.53 (Jan. 2021) following microsoft/vscode issue #70413, is wrapTabs:

"workbench.editor.wrapTabs": true

It does avoid horizontal overflow by wrapping tabs onto multiple rows.

Q: How to execute mysqldump command from the host machine to a mysql docker container A:

I did not see a correct answer to the question, so here is how to get the dump out from the container to the host, and bzip2 compressed. If you just want the dump uncompressed, then just leave out the "| bzip2"

docker exec container_id sh -c 'mysqldump --all-databases -u root -p"passwd"'| bzip2 > db_dump.sql.bz2

If you use docker compose, then run this in the directory where the compose file is located

docker compose exec container_name sh -c 'mysqldump --all-databases -u root -p"passwd"'| bzip2 > db_dump.sql.bz2

Q: How can I open csv files and read them and sort them based on the data inside it? A:

try csv.reader(Filename)

import csv
def CSV2List(csvFilename: str):
    f = open(csvFilename)
    q = csv.reader(f)
    return sorted(q,key=lambda x: x[0])

Q: How do I select a CSS element that has no attributes? A:

There is no dedicated CSS pseudo-class for selecting an element that has no attributes.

If XPath is an option, the cleanest solution is:

//section/div[not(@*)]

This selects div elements inside section that have no attributes at all.

In CSS, you generally have to explicitly exclude the attributes you know about, e.g.:

section > div:not([id], [class], [data-test-id], [aria-label])

So unfortunately, CSS doesn't have a simple equivalent of XPath's not(@*).
